# Known misspellings — soroauth spell check (issue #151)
#
# One "typo->correction" pair per line. Both sides are lowercase alphabetic
# tokens: the tokenizer case-folds and splits at lower→upper boundaries, so
# "RecieveSomething" is caught by the "recieve" row. Entries the tokenizer
# can never see (digits, punctuation) are rejected at startup — fail closed,
# never silent dead weight.
#
# Inflections: rows are base forms. The checker also matches mechanical
# English inflections of a listed row (-s, -es, -ed, -ing, -ings, -ly, and
# y->ies/ied) and inflects the correction back, so "recieves" is caught by
# the "recieve" row and suggests "receives". Stripping only extends a row
# that already exists; it cannot turn an ordinary word into a finding.
#
# Provenance: the initial list is the cross-product of the classic
# codespell "rare" and Wikipedia "commonly misspelled words" lists against
# every word that actually occurs in this repository's Markdown corpus
# (extracted with the same tokenizer and diffed against the lists), then
# manually reduced to rows with at least one real occurrence or a
# plausible near miss. Corrections follow Merriam-Webster and the Google
# developer documentation style guide. When a row's word appears in the
# corpus, the row was validated against that occurrence in context before
# being committed — see the commit body for the command and its output.
#
# Ordering: alphabetical by typo. Add new rows in the same order.
#
# Maintenance contract (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Spell-checking the
# documentation"):
#   - a row is added when a real typo is caught or corrected;
#   - a row is removed only with the corpus commit that fixed every
#     occurrence, so the file never names a typo that is currently live;
#   - never add a project term here; it belongs in words.txt.
